sections.heading: Data Types
sections.body: As explained in the Variables chapter, a variable in C must be a specified data type, and you must use a format specifier inside the printf() function to display it:

sections.heading: Example
Basic Data Types
sections.body: The data type specifies the size and type of information the variable will store. In this tutorial, we will focus on the most basic ones: Data Type Size Description Example int 2 or 4 bytes Stores whole numbers, without decimals 1 float 4 bytes Stores fractional numbers, containing one or more decimals. Sufficient for storing 6-7 decimal digits 1.99 double 8 bytes Stores fractional numbers, containing one or more decimals. Sufficient for storing 15 decimal digits 1.99 char 1 byte Stores a single character/letter/number, or ASCII values 'A'

sections.heading: Basic Format Specifiers
sections.body: There are different format specifiers for each data type. Here are some of them: Format Specifier Data Type Try it %d or %i int Try it » %f or %F float Try it » %lf double Try it » %c char Try it » %s Used for strings (text), which you will learn more about in a later chapter Try it » Note: It is important that you use the correct format specifier for the specified data type. If not, the program may produce errors or even crash.
